div.l: With hym̄ there rode a gentill Pardonere A pardonere
Of Rouncivale his felawe and his compere
That streight was comen̄ fro the Courte of Rome
Full loude he songe com̄ hither love com tome
This Sompnoure bare to hym̄ a stif Burdoıı̄un
Was neủere Trumpe of half so grete a sown̄
This pardonere had here · as yelowe as eny wex
But smothe hynge it as doith a strike of flex
By ouncis hynge his lokkys that he hadde
And therewith his shurdres it oủere spradde
But thynne it lay by culpons on̄ and on̄
And an̄ hode for Iolyte wered he non̄
For it was trussed vppe in his walette
Hym̄ thought he rode all of the newe Iette
Disshevele saue his hat he rode all bare
With glaryng yeen̄ as hath an̄ hare
A vernacle had he sewed on̄ his Cappe
His walet lay be forn̄ hym̄ in his lappe
Fret full of pardoıı̄un come fro Rome all hote
A voyce he hadde as small as hath a gote
No berde he hadde ne neủere shulde haue
As smothe it was · as it were newe shaue
I trowe he were a geldyng or a mare
But of his Crafte fro Berwik vnto ware
Ne was there suche another Pardonere
For in his male he a feyre pelowe bere
Which as he saide than̄ was oure lady veile
He saide he had eke a gobet of the seile
That seynte Petyr had when̄ that he went
Vppon̄ the See · there IħuIhesu Criste hym̄ hent
He had a Crosse of latoıı̄un full of stonys
And in a glas he had many piggis bonys
But with thise reliquys whan̄ that he fonde
A pore parsoıı̄un dwellyng vplonde
Vppon̄ a day he gate hym̄ more money
Than̄ did the parsoıı̄un in monethis twey
And thus with his feyned flatrye and Iapys
He made the parsoıı̄un and the peple his Apys
But truly to telle of hym̄ at the laste
